title: Commercial LPG up for third month; Kolkata cylinder rises Rs 17 to Rs 2,971
dek: Domestic cylinder prices were left unchanged, while jet fuel went up for a fourth month in a row.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Oil marketing companies raised the price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder from Sunday, 1 November, with Kolkata seeing the steepest increase among the four metros, Rs 17, taking the price to Rs 2,971, reports said.

In Delhi the commercial cylinder now costs Rs 2,820, up Rs 10 from Rs 2,810. In Mumbai it rose Rs 10.50 to Rs 2,775 and in Chennai Rs 11.50 to Rs 2,994.50, according to the reports. It is the third straight monthly increase for commercial cylinders, after rises on 1 September and 1 October, reports said. Reports differ on the size of the October rise, giving it as Rs 62.50 or Rs 65 in Delhi.

The price of the 14.2-kg domestic cylinder used in homes was unchanged at Rs 942 in Delhi, reports said.

Aviation turbine fuel (ATF) went up by Rs 1.37 a litre to Rs 138.50 in Delhi, the fourth monthly rise in a row, one report said. Petrol and diesel prices were not changed.

Commercial LPG is used by restaurants, hotels, canteens and hostels, so the increase lands just before the festive season. The commercial cylinder reached a record Rs 3,113.50 in Delhi in June, according to one report. The state-run oil companies revise LPG and ATF prices on the first day of each month. The Declaration could not access Indian Oil's official price list to confirm the city-wise figures.
